transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Laura Gomez (CardioHealth Head of Security), Ethan Kim (CTO), Priya Shah (Platform), Samir Desai (Legal)

Summary: quick security/compliance review focused on data residency and region pinning (US vs EU), cross-border processing and subprocessors. High-level agreement that CardioHealth needs EU-only processing for PHI-related telemetry and wants region pinning + contractual DPA language. Agreed next steps: send SOC2/ISO artifacts, subprocessor list, region-pin config example, schedule technical deep dive.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off. This is a follow up from the initial intake — we want to run through your residency requirements and make sure our region pinning and data processing flows match CardioHealth needs.
[00:18] Laura Gomez: Thanks Alex. yes, we had a few items flagged by privacy — primary ask is EU-only processing for anything considered protected health info or identifiers. non-PHI can live in US, but we need clear boundaries and auditability.
[00:35] Maya Patel: Got it. quick clarification: when you say EU-only, do you mean processing, storage, or both? also is there any plan for failover to other regions?
[00:45] Ethan Kim: Processing and storage both. We may accept cross-border for non-PHI but want strict region pinning for PHI. failover must stay within EU unless we approve in writing.
[00:55] Jordan Li: Understood. Redwood supports region pinning per-route and per-customer config — you can pin to eu-west-1 (or multiple EU regions) and we can prevent automatic fallback to US for pinned traffic. There's a couple of knobs: strict pin (no cross-border) vs preferred pin (allows fallback).
[01:12] Laura Gomez: We need strict. Also can you show where audit logs record region decisions and any fallback events? that's critical for audits.
[01:22] Maya Patel: Yes, our audit logging includes request-level metadata: tenant id, model version, region served, node id, and a fallback flag. logs are retained per policy, and we can configure retention windows. We'll share a sample log schema.
[01:35] Samir Desai: On legal side we need subprocessors list and any third party cloud providers used for EU processing. Are you using any third party infra in EU that might export data?
[01:47] Jordan Li: For Redwood private and dedicated we run in customer-selected cloud regions. For hosted, we operate in cloud providers' EU regions — typically AWS eu-west-1 and GCP europe-west1. We do use cloud-managed storage and monitoring services within those regions; we will provide a full list of subprocessors and where they are located.
[02:05] Ethan Kim: Are there any chances that keys or backups are replicated outside the EU? KMS, backups, snapshots?
[02:13] Maya Patel: Good question. For hosted, customer data at rest is encrypted and we offer customer-managed keys via KMS in the same region. Backups for EU-pinned tenants are also stored in the same region by default. We can provide a commitment in the DPA to avoid cross-region replication for pinned tenants.
[02:32] Laura Gomez: And what about logs used for debugging — do those ever go to centralized US observability or to support tools that live outside the EU?
[02:40] Alex Chen: We have a separation: for EU-pinned accounts, support and telemetry can be configured to be EU-only. we also have an option to route observability ingest to EU-only endpoints; if you want support access from outside EU, that would be a separate contractual permission.
[02:55] Priya Shah: From an engineering standpoint we need examples — API flags, headers, env config. how do we pin a given route or tenant?
[03:03] Maya Patel: You can set region_pin: eu in the account config or to a list of regions. We also surface a route-level parameter so you can pin specific endpoints. Example: POST /v1/generate with header X-Region-Pin: eu-west-1. We'll send a sample snippet.
[03:20] Laura Gomez: That header — is it enforced server-side or advisory? we want it enforced.
[03:25] Jordan Li: It's enforced for pinned tenants. there's a policy engine that validates incoming requests' tenant id against the pinned region. If a request would route outside the pinned region, it's rejected unless an override flag and recorded fallback is present.
[03:40] Ethan Kim: For failover — what if the entire EU region becomes unavailable? we need SLOs and an explicit manual override process rather than automatic spill to US.
[03:50] Maya Patel: We support automated fallback policies, but for strict pinning we recommend manual failover: we'll have a documented process and you can authorize a temporary cross-border failover in writing. we can also configure health checks and alerts to notify your ops team.
[04:05] Laura Gomez: Ok good. Next: cross-border subprocessors. Does Redwood use any analytics or monitoring vendor that might process data in the US?
[04:12] Alex Chen: We do use a few vendor services; for EU tenants we prefer EU-based vendor endpoints. we'll provide the list and mark which ones process outside EU.
[04:22] Samir Desai: We need explicit contract clause that prohibits transfer of EU personal data to countries without an adequacy decision unless we agree. Also SCCs or equivalent mechanisms must be in place.
[04:33] Jordan Li: Understood. our standard DPA includes SCCs and we can add an EU exit clause and an explicit prohibition on cross-border processing for pinned data without written permission.
[04:43] Priya Shah: On encryption: can you confirm key ownership options? BYOK (customer-managed keys) and where the KMS is hosted?
[04:50] Maya Patel: We support BYOK in supported clouds. KMS keys can be created in your cloud account (recommended) so keys don't leave your control. For Redwood-managed KMS, we can restrict key material to EU regions. We'll show both options in the docs.
[05:06] Laura Gomez: Audit logs retention — default and adjustable? We need 7 years for some audit trails. can you support that?
[05:13] Jordan Li: Retention is configurable; default is 90 days in hosted, but we offer extended retention as an add-on — up to multi-year. We'll provide pricing and retention options in the follow up.
[05:25] Ethan Kim: Are logs encrypted at rest and in transit? and are they accessible to Redwood engineers?
[05:31] Maya Patel: Yes, TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. Access to logs is role-based; engineers only get access through RBAC and SSO (SAML/OIDC). We also have just-in-time access and audit trails for any access by support or engineers.
[05:45] Laura Gomez: For SSO, we use SAML with SCIM provisioning. Any issues integrating?
[05:51] Alex Chen: We support SAML and OIDC, SCIM provisioning for users and groups, and can map roles to RBAC policies. We'll include a quickstart for SAML and SCIM configs.
[06:05] Priya Shah: One more operational detail: data ingress from integrations. Some of our connectors send PDFs with PHI to your ingestion endpoint. Are attachments included in residency constraints?
[06:15] Maya Patel: Yes, attachments and any payloads that are stored fall under the tenant's residency and pinning. We classify by tenancy and policy; if it's a pinned tenant, attachments are stored in the pinned region.
[06:25] Laura Gomez: How about subprocessor notifications — do you maintain a public list and notify customers of changes?
[06:32] Jordan Li: We maintain a living list and we notify customers of material subprocessor changes; for EU-pinned tenants we provide advance notice and, where needed, a chance to object under the DPA.
[06:44] Ethan Kim: Do you ever do staff support from outside EU where they might view logs?
[06:50] Alex Chen: Support is restricted by config. By default EU-pinned accounts restrict support access to EU-only locations. If support needs to access from other locations that's a controlled exception with customer approval and is logged in the audit trail.
[07:05] Laura Gomez: Ok that's helpful. Can you confirm SOC2 Type II scope covers hosted EU processing?
[07:11] Maya Patel: Our SOC2 report covers our hosted operations and controls across regions. we'll send the SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert in the follow up.
[07:20] Samir Desai: On legal specifics: we'd like the DPA to explicitly state that backups and disaster recovery snapshots for pinned tenants remain within EU unless we approve. Also include a clause for subprocessors and SCCs.
[07:33] Jordan Li: We can do that; we'll have legal propose language and send the DPA draft.
[07:40] Priya Shah: For the tech deep dive, we want a walkthrough of the enforcement path — policy engine, routing table, and a sample end-to-end request flow. Also want to run a smoke test with an EU-only tenant to confirm no egress.
[07:52] Maya Patel: We'll prepare a session: architecture diagram, policy enforcement flow, sample logs showing region header and enforcement decision. We can run a smoke test in a sandbox tenant with you.
[08:05] Laura Gomez: Great. anything else re: certifications or penetration testing?
[08:10] Alex Chen: We do annual pen tests and we can share a summary of findings and remediation. We also maintain ISO 27001 and will include cert.
[08:20] Ethan Kim: Timeline — we need to finalize legal and run pilot by late October, production early November. Can Redwood commit to that?
[08:29] Alex Chen: Sounds doable. We'll aim to get docs to you within a week and schedule the technical deep dive first week of October so pilot work can start mid-October.
[08:40] Laura Gomez: Ok, recap please?
[08:43] Alex Chen: Recap: 1) Alex will send SOC2/ISO and pen test summary; 2) Jordan will share subprocessors and data flow diagrams; 3) Maya will provide region-pinning config and enforcement docs + sample logs; 4) schedule tech deep dive week of Oct 4; 5) Legal exchange DPA draft with EU-only backup clause.
[09:05] Samir Desai: we'll review and come back with any objections, and Priya will coordinate the smoke test.
[09:12] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone -- we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite.

Notes on transcript quality: voice transcript had a few mislabels and minor word swaps around "KMS" and "key material" earlier; verified items will be in the written docs we send.

References mentioned: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, DPA draft, subprocessors list, region-pinning config example, sample log schema (to be shared).

End of call.
